name: 大三元
description: Three complete pung or kong sets of the dragon tiles: red, green, and white.
ruleNote: The three dragon sets may be open or concealed. Confirm whether your table requires a winning hand.
winningPotentialNote: This illustrated hand has one specific wait: the final 5 Circle completes its pair.

name: 大四喜
description: Four complete pung or kong sets of the wind tiles: east, south, west, and north.
ruleNote: This is commonly treated as a top-tier hand. Check local rules for any limit or cap that applies.
winningPotentialNote: This illustrated hand has one specific wait: the final White Dragon completes its pair.

name: 七对子
description: A concealed hand made from seven distinct pairs, rather than the usual four sets and a pair.
ruleNote: All seven pairs must be concealed. Confirm whether four-of-a-kind may count as two pairs at your table.
winningPotentialNote: This illustrated hand has one specific wait: the final White Dragon completes its seventh pair.

name: 花胡
description: A special self-draw win associated with flower-tile rules used by the table.
ruleNote: Flower-win handling varies most between groups. Use this as a baseline and update the catalogue to match your house rule.
winningPotentialNote: This example is a completed Flower Win. The exact flower and self-draw conditions depend on the table rule.

name: 天胡
description: The dealer wins immediately with the original dealt tiles, before taking a normal turn.
ruleNote: Usually limited to the first round and the dealer. Many tables pay this at the shooter rate.
winningPotentialNote: A Heavenly Hand is complete in the dealer's original tiles, so it does not use a normal draw or discard wait.

name: 地胡
description: A non-dealer wins immediately on the first opportunity before normal play develops.
ruleNote: Usually limited to the first round. Confirm your table's self-draw, robbing, and payout conditions.
winningPotentialNote: This illustrated hand has one specific wait: the final Green Dragon completes its pair on the first opportunity.

name: 十三幺
description: A concealed hand containing each terminal and honor tile once, plus one matching pair.
ruleNote: The 13 distinct tiles are 1 and 9 of every suit, all four winds, and all three dragons. Confirm your table's payout cap.
winningPotentialNote: Thirteen Wonders has 13 possible waits: any one of the 13 terminal or honor tiles can complete the pair.

name: 坎坎胡
description: A concealed hand formed from four pung sets and a pair, with no sequence sets.
ruleNote: All sets are normally concealed. Confirm whether your table allows any exposed pung or kong in this hand.
winningPotentialNote: This illustrated hand has one specific wait: the final White Dragon completes its concealed pair.

name: 十八罗汉
description: A hand with four kong sets and a pair, also known as Eighteen Arhats.
ruleNote: The four kongs expose 18 tiles in total. Check whether your table awards a higher tai value or a limit for this hand.
winningPotentialNote: This illustrated hand has one specific wait: the final Red Dragon completes the pair after four kongs.

name: 清老头
description: A hand made entirely from 1 and 9 terminal tiles, with no sequences or honor tiles.
ruleNote: Each set is a pung or kong of a terminal tile. Confirm whether your table treats this as a limit hand.
winningPotentialNote: This illustrated hand has one specific wait: the final 9 Circle completes its terminal pair.

name: 九莲宝灯
description: A concealed one-suit hand containing 1112345678999 plus any one additional tile of that suit.
ruleNote: The base pattern can win on any tile in the same suit. Confirm your table's tai value, limit, and concealed-hand requirement.
winningPotentialNote: Nine Gates has nine possible waits: any 1-9 tile in the same suit completes the base pattern.
